question: Which compound is used to neutralise fatty acids and convert them into salts in a process called saponification?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium hydroxide**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sodium hydroxide** is used to neutralise fatty acids and convert them into salts in the process called saponification.
 
• Saponification is a process that produces soap from fats or oils and a base.
 
• The reaction involves the hydrolysis of triglycerides (fatty acids) by sodium hydroxide to produce glycerol and soap.
 
• This process is essential in the production of various cleaning products and has been used for centuries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sodium hydroxide**, also known as lye or caustic soda, is a highly caustic metallic base and alkali.
 
• It is used in various industries including paper manufacturing, textiles, and cleaning agents.
 
• The chemical formula for sodium hydroxide is **NaOH**.
 
• Due to its corrosive nature, it must be handled with care, using appropriate safety measures.
